To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) dietary intake in the elderly is associated with several socio-demographic factors; (2) the elderly population consumes more energy from fat than from protein and carbohydrates; (3) the elderly consume more saturated fatty acids than poly-unsaturated ones; and (4) a higher level of education is associated with lower consumption of n-6 fatty acids.
the elderly population has a high consumption of saturated fatty acid, a low intake of monounsaturated fatty acids, and an inadequate ratio between n-6 and n-3 fatty acids.
the dietary intake of elderly French community dwellers is characterized by a low intake of protein, mono- and disaturated fatty acids and high intake of carbohydrate.
In summary, our research is concerned with

a population with a high prevalence of cardiovascular risk factors and a high consumption of saturated fat, with a low consumption of polyunsaturated fatty acids, which are major risk factors for CVD and type 2 diabetes.
the nutritional status of elderly subjects and the relationship with their socio-economic status.
the identification of the dietary patterns in the elderly, in order to propose nutritional strategies adapted to this population.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the French elderly community-dwelling population has an inadequate intake of fatty acids.
elderly people have a low intake of MUFA and a high intake of SFA and n-6 fatty acids, which could contribute to the development of chronic diseases.
the elderly population of the present study had inadequate dietary intakes, especially in terms of fatty acids.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the elderly population in Bordeaux is at risk of nutritional deficiencies and that this population should be targeted by nutritional intervention programmes.
elderly women are at risk of poor nutritional intake and that the dietary habits of the French elderly population are not optimal in terms of macronutrient distribution and fatty acid intake.
the elderly in the Bordeaux sample of Three-City study are at risk of having inadequate diets in terms of energy and macronutrient intakes and of having excess intake of SFA.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a higher intake of MUFA is required, whereas SFA intake should be limited.
the elderly population in Bordeaux, France, has a low intake of MUFA, which could have negative health consequences.
a high consumption of saturated fat and a low consumption of MUFA and n-3 PUFA should be considered as a public health problem in this French elderly population.
